statement: message = array of [Type, Data?] tuples; one array passed to ctx.down/ctx.up = one wave; in-process representation = tuple, wire representation = protobuf, decoupled at the wire-bridge boundary
rationale: D8 up/down(msgs); D11 tuple/protobuf decoupled

statement: 11 message types, CLOSED: START + DIRTY/DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR/TEARDOWN/PAUSE/RESUME/PULL. No open set, no user-defined custom types, no MessageTypeRegistry; the old unknown-type-forwarding rule is retired (vacuous under a closed set). PULL is the explicit pull-demand message; RESUME is pause-lock release only. Adding a tier/type = spec change (constitutional).
rationale: D9 9-type closed set + START handshake; D18 messageTier compile-time const, custom types CUT; D269 splits pull demand out of RESUME so parameterized pullable snapshots/retained views have a first-class control message without making DATA up-going.

statement: messageTier const table (7 tiers): 0 START(handshake) / 1 PAUSE·RESUME·PULL(control/demand) / 2 DIRTY(notification) / 3 DATA·RESOLVED(value) / 4 INVALIDATE(settle) / 5 COMPLETE·ERROR(terminal) / 6 TEARDOWN. Tiers <3 dispatch immediately; tiers ≥3 are batch-deferred (DATA/RESOLVED in the settle slice, INVALIDATE alongside, terminal after, TEARDOWN last). Closed const table — adding a tier is constitutional; D269 adds PULL to existing tier 1 and does not add a tier.
rationale: D34 ratified numbering (control precedes notification); D9 closed set; D269 adds explicit demand to the existing control tier while preserving the seven-tier table.

statement: [DATA,v] requires a non-SENTINEL payload (v ≠ undefined/None/per-language sentinel); [ERROR,e] requires an explicit non-SENTINEL, non-boolean diagnostic payload; bare [DATA]/[ERROR], [DATA,SENTINEL], [ERROR,SENTINEL], [ERROR,false], and [ERROR,true] are rejected at the dispatch boundary; binding/source adapters that receive host-language undefined/boolean failures must coerce them to a valid diagnostic payload before emitting ERROR; null is a valid DATA value (domain-level absence)
rationale: D16 SENTINEL = absence-of-DATA must stay decidable; DATA(SENTINEL) would be indistinguishable from never-emitted. D78 keeps D77 terminal metadata lightweight (`false` none, `true` COMPLETE, payload ERROR) by excluding boolean ERROR payloads, so ERROR false/true cannot collide with terminal shorthand.

statement: outside batch: one ctx.down(msgs) = one wave; inside batch: accumulation until commit = one wave

every tier-3 (DATA/RESOLVED) emission is preceded by DIRTY in the same wave; the dispatcher synthesizes a [DIRTY] prefix when the caller omits it and the node is not already dirty; raw and framed emission paths are observationally identical on the wire
rationale: glitch-free two-phase contract; D9 mechanism is impl freedom but the DIRTY-before-DATA ordering is observable

statement: DIRTY (phase 1) propagates through the entire reachable graph before DATA/RESOLVED (phase 2) begins — glitch-free diamond. Activation exemption: a compute fn's first run during subscribe() does not require a preceding DIRTY
rationale: two-phase push guarantees a fan-in node sees all settled deps before recompute

statement: diamond/fan-in: D recomputes exactly once after all changed deps settle in same wave
rationale: the spec only describes observable behavior; the mechanism (dirtyMask) is impl freedom

statement: the equals substitution (DATA→RESOLVED) fires only when there is exactly 1 DATA within the wave; 0 is irrelevant; with ≥2 they are all DATA. Within one wave at one node the tier-3 slot is ≥1 DATA XOR exactly 1 RESOLVED — never mixed (tier-3 wave exclusivity). Default equals = Object.is/is; custom equals via node opts; never invoked while cache is SENTINEL
rationale: multiple DATA yield no skip-fn benefit; exclusivity keeps cache coherent with last-delivered DATA -- RETIRED by D49 (Opt-3: no auto-equals-substitution; replaced by R-resolved-undirty)

statement: multiple settle-class messages on one node in one wave are resolved by tier-sort (DATA advances cache, a trailing INVALIDATE clears it; subscribers observe the full sequence). The sole explicit merge rule is INVALIDATE+INVALIDATE collapse (cleanup hook fires at most once). DATA+RESOLVED in the same wave on the same node is a protocol violation (R-resolved-undirty / D49)
rationale: tier ordering produces the right end-state without silently eliding messages

statement: INVALIDATE is broadcast at most once per node per wave (diamond fan-in cascades it once, not once per arriving path); an INVALIDATE arriving at an already-reset OR never-populated cache is a no-op — neither the cleanup hook nor the downstream broadcast fires again
rationale: prevents double-cleanup and wedged-DIRTY deadlock; the two reset states are observationally equivalent downstream

statement: SENTINEL = absence-of-DATA, protocol-decidable; the concrete sentinel value is per-language (TS undefined/Rust None/Py sentinel)

push-on-subscribe: in the SENTINEL state push [START]; in the dirty state push [START,DIRTY]; cached DATA is pushed to the new subscriber. START is the handshake — the first message any sink receives on a subscription, emitted before any other downstream delivery, not forwarded through intermediate nodes. EXCEPTION (R-pull / D55): a pull-mode node while QUIET pushes [START] ONLY — its cached value is NOT pushed on subscribe (it stays silent until demanded).

terminal-is-forever by default; resubscribable opt-in triggers a fresh-lifecycle reset. A late subscribe to a non-resubscribable terminal node is REJECTED (idiomatic error); to a resubscribable terminal node it resets the lifecycle (clears terminal/has-fired-once/DepRecords, drains pause lockset, re-arms first-run gate) before installing the sink. TEARDOWN does not block reset
rationale: D17; resubscribable IS the property gating late-subscribe re-activation

statement: completeWhenDepsComplete (default true): node auto-emits COMPLETE when ALL deps are TERMINAL — each dep has reached COMPLETE *or* an ABSORBED ERROR (errorWhenDepsError:false); an absorbed-error dep COUNTS as terminal-done (it is settled — no more input can arrive), it does NOT block completion (B42). Completion is 'all deps TERMINAL', NOT 'all deps Complete' and NOT 'ANY' (combineLatest semantics — fires once all sources settle). errorWhenDepsError (default true): node auto-emits ERROR when any dep errors (this auto-ERROR fires BEFORE the complete-check, so an error-terminal dep only reaches the completion logic when errorWhenDepsError:false has absorbed it). Terminal-emission operators (last/reduce) set completeWhenDepsComplete:false; rescue/catch operators set errorWhenDepsError:false and read ctx.depRecords[i].terminal explicitly. SCOPE: a dep TERMINAL = COMPLETE | ERROR; TEARDOWN is a destroy-cascade (tears the node down, not a settle) and does NOT count (B33-adjacent, out of scope). IMPL (TWO parts): (1) _allDepsComplete counts a TERMINAL dep as done — block only on a LIVE dep (TS `dep_terminal === undefined` blocks; NOT `!== true/Complete`), Rust all_deps_complete mirrors. (2) BOTH the COMPLETE receive-arm AND the absorbed-ERROR receive-arm (errorWhenDepsError:false) must check `completeWhenDepsComplete && all-deps-terminal -> COMPLETE`: the COMPLETE arm already does, but the ERROR-absorbed arm currently routes straight to _settleAfterAbsorbedTerminal/_maybeRun WITHOUT the check, so an absorbed-error dep terminating LAST would not fire the cascade — it must MIRROR the COMPLETE arm's check (Rust receive_from_dep ERROR arm same). Order-independent: whichever terminal lands last triggers the auto-COMPLETE.
rationale: effect/derived completion is the join of all deps reaching a terminal state — once every dep is terminal (Complete or absorbed-Error) no more input can arrive, so the node MUST settle (COMPLETE); rescue needs explicit terminal handling. B42 fix: the prior 'all deps Complete' (TS _allDepsComplete `tm!==true`, Rust all_deps_complete) wedged a node whose errorWhenDepsError:false dep ERRORed (terminal=payload≠Complete) — it never auto-completed even after all OTHER deps completed. Counting an absorbed-error dep as terminal-done fixes the wedge AND lets a rescue/catch operator with completeWhenDepsComplete:true auto-COMPLETE after recovery (RxJS catchError(()=>of(x)) parity). NOT hit by the landed catalog (rescue/race/sample use completeWhenDepsComplete:false so the auto-cascade is skipped → zero behavior change; a dep error on a default errorWhenDepsError:true node auto-ERRORs before the complete-check) — a pure latent-wedge fix. FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-30 on the TS-arm-green (C-17 a/b/c ts:pass) + formal (wave_deps_complete.tla TLC-green + mutation-verified) precedent, like R-terminal-settles-dirty/R-rewire; rust+py arms (C-17 rust/py) follow in CSP-6/7.

statement: ctx.up is control/demand-tier only (DIRTY/PAUSE/RESUME/PULL/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN); DATA/RESOLVED/COMPLETE/ERROR are down-only. PULL may carry pullId plus optional params, but it remains a control/demand message and is not DATA-up.
rationale: directional semantics; added in DR-5; D269 adds explicit PULL demand without relaxing the DATA down-only rule.

statement: node = thinnest primitive: holds fn handle + deps + wave state machine (dep_records, dirty_mask, pending_count, cache, status, subscribers, pause_lockset); ZERO inspection cruft. Bare node() works at the substrate level but loses naming/find/describe — those are graph-layer
rationale: D5 Node↔Graph responsibility split; thin node ports cleanly to Rust

statement: node exposes: cache (readonly getter, never throws, never triggers computation), status, down(msgs), up(msgs) (restricted to control tier per R-ctx-up), subscribe(sink)→unsubscribe. cache replaces the old get()
rationale: D5 minimal node surface; D8 up/down boundary

statement: status ∈ {sentinel, pending, dirty, settled, resolved, completed, errored}; status is the source of truth for cache freshness (dirty → stale prior value, settled/resolved → fresh, completed/errored → final). cache never throws, never computes
rationale: D5 inspection reads status not raw cache

statement: state node (no deps) retains cache across disconnect — value is intrinsic/non-volatile (ROM). Compute node (deps and/or fn) clears cache on deactivation → status sentinel (RAM); reconnect re-runs fn from scratch with cleared DepRecords
rationale: D5; compute value is a function of live subscriptions

statement: node fn = (ctx)=>void; ctx = {up(msgs), down(msgs), waveData, terminal, state, onDeactivation, onInvalidate, optional pull}. ctx.pull is present only while a pullId-holder fn is executing in response to PULL({pullId,params?}); it exposes the holder-visible PullDemand as read-only demand context and is absent for normal dep-settle, activation, pause replay, terminal, and non-pull executions. `ctx.waveData` is the ONLY raw ctx dep-value input surface (R-ctx-wave-data): a two-dimensional structure indexed as dep -> waves -> per-wave value/dirty-clear projection. `ctx.terminal[i]` is separate terminal metadata for the same invocation, NOT a value source: false = dep i did not deliver COMPLETE/ERROR, true = dep i delivered COMPLETE, any non-boolean non-SENTINEL ERROR payload = dep i delivered ERROR with that payload. R-data-payload rejects boolean ERROR payloads, so the false/true shorthand cannot collide with legal ERROR payloads. No stored `latest`, `prevData`, `latestData`, or parallel dep-value alias exists on raw ctx; any current/latest/read helper is derived from waveData plus node-owned cache/state outside the raw ctx value contract, never a second source of truth. NO return-value framing — all emission is explicit via ctx.down. Sugar (derived/effect/operator) value-level fn is wrapped to a ctx-fn in the graph layer at register time; node/producer are ctx-level (intentional tier power surface, DR-1)
rationale: D8 ctx.up/down; D27 sugar→ctx-fn conversion strictly in graph layer feeds behavioral parity; D77 removes the ambiguous raw ctx `latest`/`prevData` aliases and pins waveData as the single canonical per-wave dep value input while keeping terminal metadata separate; D78 narrows ERROR payloads so the lightweight false/true/error-payload terminal metadata shape remains collision-free. D272 pins ctx.pull as the protocol-visible holder context for PULL params without adding a second dep-value source. D278 clarifies that ctx.pull denotes a holder invocation context even when the holder chooses not to emit downstream DATA.

statement: ctx.waveData is indexed by declared dep position. `waveData[i]` is a list of wave projections delivered by dep i to THIS fn invocation; each inner projection corresponds to exactly one upstream msgs array / wave (D8). An empty outer list `waveData[i] = []` means dep i delivered NO wave to this invocation. An inner empty list represents a RESOLVED-only wave: `waveData[i] = [[]]` means one RESOLVED wave. DATA payloads are stored directly in the inner list, in order: upstream `[[DATA,1],[DATA,2],[INVALIDATE]]` projects as `[[1,2,SENTINEL]]` for that dep. INVALIDATE is represented inside the inner list by the protocol SENTINEL marker (TS `undefined`, Rust/Py sentinel equivalent); DATA(SENTINEL) is already illegal by R-data-payload, so this marker cannot collide with a legal DATA payload. DATA null remains legal and projects as `[[null]]`; DATA with empty-array payload projects as `[[[]]]`; two waves DATA null then DATA [] project as `[[null],[[]]]`. RESOLVED never appears as a DATA payload and, by R-resolved-undirty, is not mixed with DATA in the same inner wave. COMPLETE/ERROR terminal information is NOT written into waveData because it is not value data; use ctx.terminal[i] (R-fn-contract) to distinguish false/no terminal, true/COMPLETE, or a legal non-boolean ERROR payload while a dirty contribution is being cleared. Implementations may store caches or dep bookkeeping internally, but raw ctx must expose exactly one dep-value input structure: waveData. Any ergonomic read/track/current helper MUST be a pure derivation from waveData plus the implementation-owned dep cache; it MUST NOT add a second raw ctx field that can drift from waveData.
rationale: D77. The raw fn input must preserve the distinctions the protocol needs: no wave this invocation vs RESOLVED/no-occurrence vs INVALIDATE/SENTINEL-clearing vs DATA with any legal payload including null or an empty array. A single two-dimensional waveData structure avoids `latest`/`prevData` ambiguity and keeps occurrence information intact under D49; terminal is separate metadata, not a value alias. D78 keeps the false/true/error-payload terminal shape collision-free by excluding boolean ERROR payloads.

statement: two cleanup hooks: ctx.onDeactivation(fn) (release external resources on deactivation) + ctx.onInvalidate(fn) (flush on INVALIDATE). onRerun (0 callsites) and onResubscribableReset (1 callsite → absorbed by ctx.state lifecycle) are cut. fn return value is freed for sugar mapping. PER-RUN LIFECYCLE (D28 clarification): both hook lists are CLEARED before each fn invocation and re-registered by the fn body — only the LATEST run's registrations are live (React effect-cleanup model). A re-run SUPERSEDES the prior run's hooks; superseded registrations are DISCARDED WITHOUT firing (consistent with the cut onRerun — there is no fire-on-rerun hook). So after K fn runs, an INVALIDATE fires onInvalidate exactly once (the current run's), and deactivation fires onDeactivation exactly once (NOT K times). Contract: a fn must (re-)register its cleanup on EVERY run that needs it (a registration guarded to a single run is dropped on the next run). A single-run node keeps its single registration (no re-run = no clear). deactivate() fires the live onDeactivation hooks then clears both lists.
rationale: D28; internal state reset belongs to ctx.state lifecycle, cleanup hooks only manage external resources + INVALIDATE. Per-run clear (D28 clarification) fixes the push-only accumulation bug surfaced by the CSP-5 Rust /qa (finding E, parity-consistent in both arms): re-registering each run grew the hook list unbounded and fired K stale hooks on the K-th INVALIDATE. Uniform clear-and-re-register for BOTH hooks (user-approved 2026-05-29); discard-without-firing keeps D28's onRerun-cut (fire-on-rerun would resurrect it).

statement: ctx.state = per-node private cross-wave state (implicit OK — node-private, not shared). Default fresh-lifecycle wipe; ctx.state.persist(on?) keeps across lifecycle. Shared/observable state must be an explicit node + dep (not ctx.state). INVALIDATE is lifecycle-continue (not fresh-lifecycle) so it does NOT wipe ctx.state — manual flush via onInvalidate
rationale: D23 private state OK, shared memory explicit; D29 fresh-lifecycle wipe + persist

statement: compute fn first-fires only after every declared dep has settled (delivered ≥1 real DATA this or a prior wave) under partial:false — producing one combined initial wave. partial:true turns the gate OFF (fn fires as soon as dirty-dep-count hits 0; fn body MUST guard SENTINEL per dep). terminalAsRealInput:true also lets a dep terminal settle the gate (Reduce-class). The gate is first-run-only (has-called-fn-once); INVALIDATE does not re-arm it; a resubscribable terminal reset does
rationale: clean multi-dep activation handshake without phantom partial waves

statement: initial (non-SENTINEL): pre-populates cache and a source pushes [DATA,initial] on subscribe; first emit runs equals against initial. Absent/undefined initial → cache holds SENTINEL, no push-on-subscribe, first emit is always DATA. INVALIDATE and resetOnTeardown return cache to SENTINEL
rationale: D16 sentinel semantics; initial is T|null never T|undefined

statement: dynamicNode = node construction variant (NOT a verb): declares a superset of all possible deps at construction, fn reads a subset per invocation via track(dep). All declared deps participate in wave tracking; an unread dep's update fires the fn (a ctx-fn with explicit ctx.down). The fn DECIDES whether to propagate: it inspects which deps delivered waves via ctx.waveData[i] (R-ctx-wave-data) and either re-emits via ctx.down (DATA) OR early-returns to stay QUIET, in which case the substrate synthesizes ONE undirty RESOLVED (D49: RESOLVED = UNDIRTY) that clears the downstream dirty WITHOUT a redundant DATA (D53). The suppress-vs-propagate decision on an unread-dep change is use-case-dependent, so it belongs to the fn (D53), NOT an automatic substrate read-mask (REJECTED D53 -- it would hard-code one policy and be the lone exception to D49's opt-in-dedup-everywhere). A downstream distinctUntilChanged remains an alternative for value-based dedup. track() is a pure per-invocation value-reader derived from ctx.waveData plus the implementation-owned dep cache; it is NOT a stored raw ctx `latest` field. Same first-run gate as static nodes. Intra-graph only — cross-graph deps go through the wire bridge (no inter-graph dynamicNode)
rationale: D35 distinct from rewire (per-invocation read-selection vs dep-set mutation); D22 bounds tracked deps to one causal domain; D77 replaces depRecords.latest/batch wording with the single raw ctx waveData contract

statement: PAUSE/RESUME carry a lock_id; lockset semantics: a true resume occurs only when every lock has RESUMEd; same-id is idempotent; RESUME of an unknown lock is a no-op at the final terminus. The routing of a RESUME for a pause lock NOT held HERE is governed by R-up-routing -- it may forward up the declared cone to find a pause-lock holder (release-if-held-else-forward-up), then drops at the depless-source terminus if no node up the cone holds the lock. RESUME never fires pull demand, never delivers pull params, and never releases a pull demand latch; PULL owns that demand path. The held-release/idempotent/every-lock-resumed lockset semantics above are unchanged.

pausable {true | 'resumeAll' | false}. true (default): skip fn while any lock held, fire fn once on final-lock RESUME with latest dep values; a leaf source's (depless) own external down() -- sync OR async (timer tick / promise resolve / state.set) -- is NOT gated in default mode (delivered immediately). 'resumeAll': buffer the node's own tier-3/4 settle slice while paused (incl a leaf source's own sync/async down()), replay per-entry in arrival order on final-lock RESUME against a pre-pause baseline (equals references the conceptual-timeline cache); tier-5/6 bypass the buffer. false: ignore PAUSE/RESUME ENTIRELY (timer sources that must keep producing) -- the lockset is never consulted, neither dep-driven recompute nor any (sync/async) own production is gated or buffered. pausable mode is the OUTER gate over R-async-paused (D44): an async-pool late emit buffers ONLY when pausable in {true,'resumeAll'} AND (for true) the node is a COMPUTE node (deps>0); a depless async leaf source delivers immediately in true mode (leaf-vs-compute discriminator = deps.length===0). The ORTHOGONAL pull axis (NodeOptions.pullId:<id>, R-pull / D269) sits ON TOP of pausable mode: a pull node is quiet-by-default behind a pullId demand latch and RE-QUIETS after each PULL demand; while quiet it suppresses the downstream DIRTY relay + push-on-subscribe; the pausable mode then determines the DEMAND DELIVERY CONTENT (true -> coalesced latest; 'resumeAll' -> buffered backlog drained). pull+pausable:false is REJECTED because pull needs the pausable delivery-content axis and quiet gating, not because RESUME is the demand signal.
rationale: PAUSE is backpressure on recomputation/propagation; production-gating is resumeAll's job. D44 pins the precedence over R-async-paused -- production is gated only by resumeAll, never by true/false (formal wave_async_paused.tla: ShouldBuffer + NoBufferWhenIgnoring, TLC-green across true/false/leaf/resumeAll + mutation-verified). D55 adds the orthogonal pull axis (delivery-content = mode); D269 changes the trigger from RESUME to explicit PULL while preserving the delivery-content matrix.

statement: an async result arriving at a paused node buffers and replays on final-lock RESUME -- BUT this is GATED by pausable mode (D44), not unconditional: it applies only when pausable in {true,'resumeAll'} and, in true mode, only to a COMPUTE node (deps>0). A pausable:false node never buffers (ignores PAUSE, keeps producing); a true-mode depless leaf source delivers its own async production immediately (R-pause-modes). The buffered result enters the node-level pause_lockset-scoped buffer (lock_id scope = node-level pause_lockset).
rationale: DR-3; D44 conditions the buffering on pausable mode + node kind -- the C-2 node is an async COMPUTE node (deps>0), which is why it buffers; pausable:false (B20) and the async leaf source (B20's twin) are the cases the unconditional reading got wrong.

statement: a [[TEARDOWN]] arriving at a non-terminal node synthesizes a [COMPLETE] prefix in the same wave ([[COMPLETE],[TEARDOWN]]) so bridge subscribers resolve before unwiring. Idempotent (subsequent TEARDOWN arrives alone); skipped when the wave already carries COMPLETE/ERROR
rationale: clean complete-then-teardown lifecycle pair; firstValueFrom-style bridges need the COMPLETE

statement: replayBuffer:N → node keeps a circular buffer of the last N outgoing DATA values; a late subscriber receives buffered DATA after the START handshake and before live updates
rationale: replaces the replay() operator + subscribe-hook monkeypatching

statement: restore/hydration is a graph lifecycle operation, NOT a fresh-lifecycle transition and NOT a sync-core I/O operation. Async loading, decoding, storage reads, and WAL/diff materialization happen outside the sync wave core; the resolved checkpoint commits at a graph boundary as one bootstrap/batch restore transaction. Restore restores the checkpointed graph state: all serialized ctx.state (including non-persist state), serialized caches/value absence, terminal/lifecycle state when represented, topology/factory bindings, and collection backendState when a D160 collection-owned contributor is present. It MUST NOT wipe ctx.state, reset serialized restored caches to SENTINEL, re-arm first-run as if never run, fire fresh-lifecycle cleanup hooks merely because a checkpoint was restored, or mutate a live graph invisibly behind subscribers. Reactive collection snapshot/helper caches are non-authoritative D160 derived views; restore ignores any such cached DATA and seeds the collection from backendState. After ready/commit, restored cached values participate in normal push-on-subscribe: a late subscriber to a restored dep-bearing/derived node receives that node's restored cache directly, and dependency activation/push-on-subscribe caused by reconnecting restored topology MUST NOT by itself recompute, overwrite, or clear the restored cache. Post-commit upstream DATA/INVALIDATE/terminal events are ordinary waves and may update restored nodes normally. Incremental restore/diff replay, when supported, applies changes through the normal graph boundary/wave machinery rather than direct hidden state mutation. A restore with a missing or local-only factory reference fails honestly; it does not synthesize placeholder function bodies.
rationale: D83 closes DS-1 Flag 1: restore is state-preserving, while wipe occurs only on an actual fresh-lifecycle reset (R-terminal resubscribable reset / deactivation lifecycle). D117 closes the restored-derived late-subscribe ambiguity: checkpointed serialized cache/state is load-bearing, and restored topology activation is not a hidden recompute pass. D160 makes collection backendState the authority for reactive collections and treats collection snapshot/helper caches as derived non-authoritative views. D57 keeps hydration's async work outside F-SYNC-CORE, and D82 keeps storage/WAL/envelope APIs in the binding layer. The protocol obligation is the observable lifecycle: a restored graph resumes from the checkpointed graph state and any live/diff observers see restore effects only through graph-boundary ordering, not hidden mutation.

statement: snapshot/checkpoint captures the graph's live inspectable topology (the same current/live dep + mount path truth source as R-describe/R-edges-derived), each restorable node's factory reference/name, cache/value state including SENTINEL absence, terminal/lifecycle state when represented, and ALL node-private ctx.state regardless of ctx.state.persist flags. Reactive collection snapshot/helper caches are the D160 exception: they are non-authoritative derived views of the collection backend, so checkpoint records them as SENTINEL/absence while the collection-owned backendState contributor is authoritative. Function bodies are never serialized; restore re-resolves nodes by factory reference through the dispatcher/graph factory registry. Anonymous inline or unregistered functions are marked local-only and cannot restore cross-process; missing factory refs fail restore honestly. Snapshot records may carry incremental changeset/diff intent, but storage tiers, WAL frame shape, codecs, content addressing, and durability policy are presentation/binding-layer concerns, not substrate rules.
rationale: D25 pins factory-name refs because fn bodies cannot serialize; D51/R-describe pins live topology as the truthful graph snapshot source after rewire; D83 adds the explicit ctx.state/cache/lifecycle payload and local-only failure contract. D160 keeps reactive collection backends as the single materialized authority and makes snapshot node caches non-authoritative derived views; checkpoint therefore stores collection backendState rather than duplicating collection snapshot caches. D82 deliberately keeps storage substrate and WAL/diff codecs separate from graph restore semantics.

statement: Graph = convenience + inspection entry: register/name/find/describe/observe/profile/snapshot/mount/batch/operators. g.* sugar desugars to dispatcher.register + Node + auto-registers into the graph inspection index. Graph is optional convenience, not a mandatory container; multi-graph is natural
rationale: D5 Graph holds all convenience+inspection; D3 graph-first mental anchor

statement: edges are derived on-demand from each node's CURRENT/LIVE deps (the node's live _deps, RE-READ at describe() call time — NOT a construction-time snapshot, so a rewire C-8/C-11 is reflected; D51) + the mount hierarchy; there is no stored edge registry and no connect/disconnect. Every edge shown in describe has a real protocol subscription behind it — decorative edges are not representable (the live-deps reading is what KEEPS this true post-rewire: a construction-time edge would be decorative after unsubscribeDep). A live dep absent from the graph inspection index (a runtime *Map inner / bare graph-less node) is auto-discovered as a snapshot node, factory from its NodeOptions.factory (R-describe); auto-discovery follows transitive live reachability through unregistered deps, so an auto-discovered inner's own current deps are also emitted as nodes+edges when reachable.
rationale: D3 topology is a pure function of (nodes, CURRENT deps, mounts); D51 — 'construction-time deps' self-contradicted 'every edge has a real subscription' once rewire (D42/D47) made topology dynamic (a unsubscribeDep'd construction edge is decorative after unsubscribeDep). Live-deps reading restores truthfulness + realizes D47/C-11 'describe shows currently-live inners'. B38 resolves the D51 follow-up by treating auto-discovery as a live-reachability walk rather than a one-level leaf capture, preserving edge truthfulness for composed graph-less inners.

statement: replaceDeps/subscribeDep/unsubscribeDep = runtime topology rewire, INTRA-graph only (D22 single causal domain; no inter-graph form — cross-graph wiring is only via the wire bridge). Surgical/Option-C: a dep in both old and new sets is left untouched (subscription + DepRecord survive); only removed deps unsubscribe + discard their DepRecord, only added deps fresh-subscribe; DepRecord-ref dispatch lets kept deps reorder freely. Across a rewire: the first-run gate (_hasCalledFnOnce) is PRESERVED, never re-armed (re-arming would re-gate unchanged deps); an added dep enters prevData=SENTINEL and the fn guards via prevData===SENTINEL; the activated compute-node cache is PRESERVED (R-rom-ram); pause lockset + buffer PRESERVED. An added dep with a cached DATA pushes [DIRTY,DATA] on subscribe (R-push-subscribe); a SENTINEL dep delivers START only. unsubscribeDep clears the removed dep's dirty contribution; if it was the sole dirty contributor and the node was dirty, the wave auto-settles. A removed dep's queued messages (DIRTY/DATA/INVALIDATE) are DRAINED — nothing strands downstream. Rejects: self-dependency; a cycle (DFS O(V+E)); a terminal this (completed/errored) for IMMEDIATE/external rewire; adding a non-resubscribable terminal dep (would wedge — resubscribable terminal deps are allowed). Deferred self-rewire queued before terminal is the D62 exception: R-rewire-deferred may apply subscribeDep/unsubscribeDep/replaceDeps after the owner becomes terminal, while terminal remains an output guard. unsubscribeDep to zero deps is allowed (degenerate fn-no-deps; cache preserved; no auto-deactivate). Mid-wave rewire (between dep deliveries) is allowed; mid-fn rewire (while the node's fn is executing, _insideRunWave) and reentrant rewire (another replaceDeps/subscribeDep/unsubscribeDep in flight) are REJECTED — a fn mutating its own topology mid-wave is the synchronous feedback-cycle ERROR (D37/R-reentrancy). Topology change does not bump a version counter (topology ≠ DATA). Every rewire API requires an explicit fn (fn-deps pairing: user fns read data[i]/prevData[i] positionally, so a dep-shape change must re-declare the fn). A SELF-triggered mutation (a fn changing its OWN deps in response to its own data) must use the deferred ctx.rewireNext path (R-rewire-deferred / D47), NOT an immediate in-fn call.
rationale: D42 ratifies the TLA+-verified (port-model wave_protocol_rewire, 126k states) rewire design Q1–Q7 for the clean-slate substrate; D22 bounds it to one causal domain; the mid-fn reject is floor-mandated by D37/R-reentrancy; surgical/Option-C + required-fn come from the Phase 13.8 design iteration. D62 narrows the terminal-this reject to immediate/external rewire only: queued self-rewire drains after terminal, with terminal sealing output rather than freezing topology. Per D42 SD-2, the cross-axis formal coverage is COMPLETE (wave_rewire.tla INVALIDATE+terminal + wave_rewire_emit.tla equals+multi-sink, all TLC-green + mutation-verified) and the TS C-8 arm is green; flipped ACTIVE 2026-05-28 on the TS-arm-green+formal precedent (R-reentrancy/R-up-at-source/R-dirty-before-data), rust/py conformance arms tracked separately in C-8 runtimes

statement: graph.mount(subgraph,{at}) embeds a child graph addressable under the parent namespace (:: delimited paths); lifecycle signals propagate parent→mounted children; mount has no deps (exempt from deps-first ordering)
rationale: D4 mount verb; L4-Q4 mount exemption

statement: describe(opts?) = static, JSON-serializable structure snapshot: {name?; nodes:DNode[]; edges:{from,to}[]; subgraphs?}. DNode = {id (stable mount-aware :: path, auto-numbered when unnamed), name?, factory (operator real name per D6/L1.5, not 'derived'), status (R-status-enum), value? (field ABSENT = SENTINEL/never-emitted), deps:id[], meta? (static annotations, R-meta-presentation)}. edges are derived from each node's CURRENT/LIVE deps + the mount hierarchy (R-edges-derived / D51) — re-read at call time, so a rewire (C-8 immediate / C-11 *Map deferred) is reflected (the snapshot is point-in-time live, NOT a construction snapshot). A live dep absent from the graph index (a runtime *Map inner / bare graph-less node) is AUTO-DISCOVERED as a snapshot node: synthesized stable id, status/value from the node getters, factory from its OWN NodeOptions.factory (the field D43 reserved for standalone graph-less operators, set by the free initNode) else '?'; auto-discovered inners are NOT persistently registered in the graph index (best-effort live capture, no register/unregister churn — D51 chose B2 over a persistent registry). Auto-discovery is a transitive live-reachability walk: after the registered-node pass, every discovered unregistered node is recursively expanded through its own CURRENT/LIVE deps, emitting reachable unregistered nodes+edges with stable synthesized ids; cycles are represented by edges but each discovered node is emitted once per snapshot. value carries the cache snapshot at call time; fn bodies are never serialized (factory-name ref only, D25). describe({explain:{from,to}}) = causal-chain subset (same shape, filtered to the from→to chain). Renderers (pretty/mermaid/d2) are pure functions over the snapshot — NOT methods and NOT a describe({format}) option; there is no graph.explain(). Live-topology streaming (rewire deltas) is an observe topology-event, deferred to CSP-2 viz
rationale: D3 describe first-class; D39 pins the field set; L4-Q8 renderers pure fns; D25 snapshot same source; per-language (D24, never in parity — documented contract, not conformance-tested); D51 — the snapshot reflects LIVE deps (truthful post-rewire) + auto-discovers unregistered inners (factory via the D43-reserved NodeOptions.factory); B38 closes the D51 transitive-discovery follow-up by making auto-discovery a live-reachability walk rather than a one-level leaf capture; live-topology STREAMING (deltas) stays deferred to viz (a point-in-time read is not streaming)

statement: observe(path?) = read-only live message tap returning a subscribable EGRESS ({subscribe(sink)→unsubscribe}) — NOT a graph node (no self-observation island). observe is a REAL (lazily-activating) subscriber: it uses subscribe internally, so observing a COLD node activates it + its upstream (running their fns), and observing a cached node receives the [DATA,cached] push (R-push-subscribe). 'Read-only' (D19) means observe never EMITS or MUTATES node state — it does NOT mean activation-free; observing a cold graph activates it. Each stream item is an enveloped ObserveEvent = {path, msg (the Message), tier (messageTier), seq (graph-local monotonic clock, D26)}; the envelope carries node identity so single-node / subtree / whole-graph observe share ONE shape. Upstream control is a separate Graph affordance: single-node up(msgs) / all-nodes up(path,msgs) (e.g. PAUSE). Clean-slate observe has no Actor, per-node guard or silent authorization filter; product access is an explicit graph-visible authorization boundary under D620.
rationale: D5 Graph IS the introspection layer; D39 pins the ObserveEvent envelope + read-only egress (not a node); D19 inspection read-only; D620 retires archived per-node Actor/guard authorization; per-language (D24, never in parity)

statement: inspection surface = describe (incl explain mode) + observe + profile — 3 first-class methods on Graph; no separate Inspector object
rationale: L4-Q8 inspection consolidation

statement: meta companion stores are presentation/graph-layer, NOT substrate. Static annotations (description/type/range/format/access/tags/unit) → describe metadata attached via g.node opts. Reactive annotations (a status/error that changes over time) → explicit nodes + dep (R-ctx-state / D23). The substrate node carries zero meta machinery. owner/access metadata is descriptive presentation material only and never ABAC enforcement, permission truth, admission or authority; product access is an explicit graph-visible authorization boundary under D620.
rationale: D36; D5 node=thinnest, meta is annotation feeding describe (graph owns inspection); D620 removes the archived per-node ABAC ambiguity

statement: graph.signal(msgs) broadcasts a message to all registered nodes (e.g. [[PAUSE,lockId]] or [[INVALIDATE]]); graph.destroy() broadcasts [[TEARDOWN]]. graph.set(name,v) = node.down([[DATA,v]]) sugar; graph.get(name) = cache read
rationale: D5 graph convenience; L4-Q1 state.set = node.down sugar

statement: monotonic time = a graph-local counter (causal-domain ordering, folded into the graph); wall-clock = a system call; there is NO global clock singleton
rationale: D26 / L3-Q9 config dissolution; graph = single-thread concurrency domain so ordering is domain-local (refined 2026-05-31 with D22 option-A; was 'causal domain', see R-graph-domain)

statement: all fn go through the dispatcher / FactoryRegistry; node((ctx)=>...) also runs through the LocalSync pool. There is no inline-fn-bypasses-dispatcher path
rationale: F-DISPATCH-ALL; sacred L0.7 (all fn through dispatcher)

statement: dispatcher.invoke is sync void — wave-state mutation always serializes onto the graph's single thread; async/remote execution returns via a pool callback. 1.0 pools = LocalSync + LocalAsync; dispatcher keeps a pluggable pool trait for WorkerPool/RemotePool
rationale: F-SYNC-CORE; D20 pool set; sacred L0.7 (wave protocol impl is sync)

statement: handle = pure data (pool_id, handle_id), NO methods — serializable/snapshottable/wire-transferable; it is a dispatcher-table index. node ≠ handle (node has up/down methods at the external-world boundary)
rationale: D7 handle is pure data

statement: graph = single-thread CONCURRENCY domain (the unit of concurrency, NOT the bound of causal influence). In-domain propagation is ONE synchronous causal wave: same-tick, glitch-free, diamonds RESOLVED-merged so a fan-in sees one consistent version of its source. Causal influence is NOT bounded by the graph — it CROSSES domains via the async wire bridge as DELAYED CONSISTENCY (a value produced in wave N is consumed one tick later in the peer domain; the two-phase wire gate preserves cross-domain consistency — wave_xgraph.tla L2.F). Compute parallelism is via pool callback (results serialize back to the domain's thread); true parallelism is via multiple graphs + wire bridge. Disjoint waves in the same graph do not parallelize (one concurrency domain = one dispatcher).
rationale: D22 wave protocol is lock-free because the graph boundary is the CONCURRENCY boundary. Wording refined 2026-05-31 (D22 option-A in-place edit; SESSION-reactive-linear-and-git M4): 'causal domain = concurrency domain' conflated two things — causal influence spans the wire bridge, so the graph bounds the concurrency unit, not the causal range; cross-domain causal propagation is delayed-consistency (wave_xgraph.tla L2.F two-phase gate). Behavior unchanged (C-1/C-4 unaffected).

statement: state changes propagate reactively via messages; never poll a node's value on a timer or busy-wait for status; periodic behavior is a reactive timer source emitting through the graph
rationale: spec §5.8 durable value

statement: no imperative side-channel triggers (event emitters, callbacks, setTimeout+set) to drive graph behavior; all coordination uses ctx.up signals + message flow through topology; remove imperative paths when no caller depends on them
rationale: spec §5.9 durable value (feedback_no_imperative)

statement: no bare async primitives in the reactive layer (TS: Promise/queueMicrotask/setTimeout/process.nextTick; PY: asyncio.create_task/threading.Timer/raw coroutines). Async boundaries live only in sources (fromPromise/fromAsyncIter) and the pool/runner layer
rationale: spec §5.10; F-SYNC-CORE async only at pool/wire boundary

statement: all data propagation — including initial values at connection time — flows through messages [[DATA,v]]; nodes do not peek a dep's .cache to seed computation; .cache is a read-only accessor for external consumers
rationale: spec §5.12 single mental model: if data moved, a message carried it

statement: protocol internals (DIRTY/RESOLVED/bitmask) never surface in the value-level primary API (derived/effect/operator); ctx-level primitives (node/producer) intentionally expose tier as a power surface (DR-1 §5.11 amend). A developer using value-level sugar never reads the spec to start
rationale: DR-1 ctx-level is a deliberate protocol-facing power surface; value-level is §5.11-compliant primary

statement: a synchronous feedback cycle — a node fn that, during its invocation, transitively re-drives one of its own (direct or indirect) deps so the same node's fn would re-enter before its wave completes — is a wave-level protocol ERROR. Detection is node-local and free: a node refuses to enter its fn-run while its own in-wave flag (_insideRunWave) is already set, and throws; the graph layer catches the throw and converts it to [[ERROR, e]] down (D30 — value-level throw → graph-layer ERROR), located at a node ON the cycle (the value-level catch nearest the throw on the synchronous unwind — implementation-determined, NOT necessarily the re-entered node), aborting the wave. The core neither queues nor bounds-then-runs the cycle (reject, not iterate). Legitimate accumulation uses per-node ctx.state (e.g. scan): not a topological cycle, never re-enters. Async feedback that crosses a turn boundary via an async pool is out of scope — it is not synchronous re-entry and does not desync the wave. No numeric rerun-depth cap is needed (precise in-wave flag detection supersedes the blunt maxFnRerunDepth)
rationale: D37; surfaced by CSP-1 /qa (backlog B10); reject (B) over queue-to-wave-end (A) because A normalizes imperative-control-flow-as-topology (feedback_no_imperative) and does not root-fix; detection reuses the existing _insideRunWave flag, dispatcher stays a pure funnel (F-DISPATCH-ALL), error ownership graph-level (D30)

statement: a depless source is the terminus of upstream control forwarding (R-ctx-up). It self-ACTS only on a message with a coherent round-trip action: INVALIDATE -> HONOR the invalidate-request (clear cache to SENTINEL, fire onInvalidate, broadcast INVALIDATE downstream = self _invalidate; the down-cascade clears the reachable downstream cone). DIRTY -> DROP/no-op (a source has no downstream-driven recompute; self-dirty would wedge downstream awaiting a settle that never arrives). TEARDOWN -> DROP/no-op (source lifecycle is source/graph-owned; revisit on a real cascade-teardown-up consumer). Dep-bearing intermediate nodes never self-act on upstream control -- they forward toward deps only; the source is the single actor and the down-cascade is the effect (D59/R-up-routing). A forwarded RESUME for a pause lock this depless source does NOT hold drops at the terminus. A forwarded PULL whose pullId this depless source does NOT hold drops at the terminus, like DIRTY; a source that DOES hold the pullId (a pull source) consumes the PULL, receives params, and fires one pull delivery if it has pending change (R-pull). Dep-bearing intermediates forward unheld RESUME/PULL up toward deps according to R-up-routing, never self-acting. D620 removes the unsupported archived per-node guard opt-out without changing these terminus actions.
rationale: D38 pins coherent source terminus actions; D59 added upstream routing; D269 splits PULL demand from RESUME so a source terminus can drop unknown demand without treating RESUME as pull; D620 removes only the unimplemented per-node guard carve-out.

statement: profile(opts?) = opt-in accumulated-counter snapshot: {waves; nodes:Record<path, NodeProfile>}, NodeProfile = {invokes, emits, resolved, errored, lastDurationNs?, totalDurationNs?}. Counters are backed by an opt-in dispatcher/graph-level recorder (DS-1 inspectorEnabled / globalInspector→dispatcher hook), NEVER stored on the thin node (R-node-thin); the dispatcher is the invoke funnel (F-DISPATCH-ALL) so it is the natural source of invoke counts + fn duration. Default OFF = zero runtime overhead (F-PERF). profile is a point-in-time snapshot (like describe); a streaming profile is an observe-aggregation, not a new mechanism. Shares the mount-aware :: path key with describe/observe
rationale: D39; L4-Q8 third inspection method; R-node-thin keeps counters off the node; F-DISPATCH-ALL dispatcher sees every invoke; F-PERF opt-in; per-language (D24, never in parity)

statement: A node fn may, DURING its run, request a mutation of its OWN dep set via ctx.rewireNext(op), op in {subscribeDep(node,fn) | unsubscribeDep(node,fn) | replaceDeps(nodes,fn)} (R-rewire surgical/Option-C semantics, D42). The request is QUEUED, not applied in place; the dispatcher DRAINS the queue at the COMMITTED wave boundary — after the current wave settles, and after a batch() commits or the final-lock RESUME (never on an un-committed or paused view) — applying each mutation as a fresh wave. Drain order is deterministic: per-node FIFO in issue order, nodes drained in causal order. This deferral is the ONLY legal self-triggered rewire: IMMEDIATE in-fn self-rewire remains the D37 mid-fn feedback-cycle ERROR (R-reentrancy); rewireNext moves application to a turn boundary where _insideRunWave is false. An added dep with cached DATA pushes [DIRTY,DATA] on the boundary wave (R-push-subscribe); a removed dep is unsubscribed and DRAINED, and if it loses its last subscriber it _deactivates and fires onDeactivation (input-side teardown — the basis for operator cancellation / abortInFlight). The first-run gate is PRESERVED across a deferred rewire (never re-armed, R-rewire). If the node goes terminal during the wave, its pending rewireNext queue is still drained: terminal is an output/lifecycle guard, NOT a deferred-topology cancellation condition. Applied subscribeDep/unsubscribeDep/replaceDeps may change live deps after terminal, but terminal status remains final and no post-terminal downstream DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR may escape; non-resubscribable late subscribe is still rejected by R-terminal, while a resubscribable reset starts the next lifecycle from the current drained dep set. A rewireNext producing no net dep-set change is a no-op; a net-changing rewireNext re-issued every boundary (oscillation) is a user-level runaway (like an infinite producer), not a substrate-detected error. The wave-boundary drain ALSO hosts a SELF-TRIGGERED DEMAND — a CONE-ROUTED PULL({pullId, params?}) demand to a pull-mode node (R-pull / R-up-routing / D269), not only dep-set mutations — for the same D37-avoidance reason (an immediate in-fn demand whose delivery loops back re-enters the consumer); same committed-boundary drain, same deferral semantics. INTRA-graph only (D22).
rationale: D47 locks deferred self-boundary work; D55/D59 reused this boundary for self-triggered pull demand; D269 changes the demand message from RESUME(pullId) to explicit PULL({pullId, params?}) while preserving committed-boundary timing.

statement: A queued self-triggered boundary task from ctx.rewireNext(op) or ctx.upNext(msgs) MUST apply only on a committed, unpaused boundary view. If requested while an outer batch is open, the pending batched tier-3/4 settle slice commits first against the pre-task topology/fn shape; the queued task drains only after the outermost batch commits, as a fresh boundary wave. If that batch rolls back explicitly, throws before commit, or fails before it is marked committed, all boundary tasks whose cause belongs to that uncommitted batch are discarded: no dep topology mutation, added-dep activation/push-on-subscribe, unsubscribeDep cleanup, replaceDeps, or self-demand PULL effect survives the rollback. The already-visible DIRTY from the rolled-back batch is balanced by the normal rollback RESOLVED (R-resolved-undirty). If the owner remains paused when the current wave settles, the queued task does not drain on the paused view; it waits until the final-lock RESUME releases the owner, then drains as a fresh boundary wave, provided any owning batch committed. Implementations MUST NOT mutate dep topology, route a self-demand, activate an added dep, or replay added-dep cached DATA while the requesting node is still inside its fn, while the batch view is uncommitted or rolled back, or while the owner is still paused. This rule remains intra-graph only (D22); D269 changes the self-demand message shape to PULL but not the committed-boundary gates.
rationale: B24 closes the cross-axis gap left by C-11. D47 locks deferred self-triggered boundary work; D67 locks batch commit-before-rewire for external/immediate rewire; D110 locks rollback fate for self-boundary tasks. D269 revises the self-demand payload from RESUME(pullId) to PULL({pullId, params?}); rollback and pause gates are unchanged.

statement: RESOLVED is the UNDIRTY / no-occurrence settle: a node DIRTY'd in phase 1 that produces NO tier-3 value this wave emits exactly one RESOLVED to clear the downstream dirty (filter-reject / no-emit fn, zero-dep un-dirty, INVALIDATE at a never-populated cache, batch-rollback DIRTY-balance). RESOLVED NEVER substitutes for a DATA and NEVER signals 'value unchanged' -- every value-occurrence is emitted as DATA regardless of value-equality (no auto-equals-substitution; the substrate does not inspect per-wave DATA count for substitution). The undirty RESOLVED is SUBSTRATE-SYNTHESIZED: a value-level operator simply returns without emitting and the substrate emits the balancing RESOLVED (R-primary-api-clean -- operator bodies carry no protocol tier); an operator MAY emit its own DATA/RESOLVED explicitly as an escape hatch. Tier-3 wave exclusivity holds: one node's settle this wave is >=1 DATA (occurrence) XOR exactly 1 RESOLVED (undirty), never mixed. RESOLVED is preceded by DIRTY in the same wave (R-dirty-before-data) like DATA. Dedup (suppress an unchanged emission / skip an expensive recompute) is OPT-IN at the operator layer (distinctUntilChanged / fn early-return), never a substrate behavior; NodeOptions.equals does not exist.
rationale: D49 supersedes D15/R-equals: equals-absorption overloaded RESOLVED (occurrence-unchanged vs dirty-clear) and destroyed occurrence info, breaking event-counting operators. Narrowing RESOLVED to undirty-only keeps occurrences as DATA (take/scan/snapshot correct) and simplifies the emit path. Glitch-free diamond (R-two-phase/R-diamond) is orthogonal and preserved.

statement: INVALIDATE × PAUSE precedence (default/'true' mode). A dep's INVALIDATE arriving while a compute node N is paused: (1) PROPAGATES downstream immediately (consistent with immediate DIRTY — not buffered in default mode; the downstream's N-DIRTY is balanced by this INVALIDATE's dirty-clear); (2) SUPERSEDES that dep's buffered paused dep-wave — N clears the dep to SENTINEL + drops its pending change, then re-derives the pending-recompute flag from whether ANY dep still carries a buffered value-change (ATTRIBUTED). On final-lock RESUME N recomputes once with the latest dep values ONLY if some dep still has a live buffered change; if none remains the recompute is CANCELLED (N already settled to SENTINEL via its own INVALIDATE — it never recomputes against an all-SENTINEL dep set). A later DATA on the same dep re-arms the buffer ([DATA,INVALIDATE,DATA2] → recompute with DATA2). resumeAll mode buffers+replays tier-3/4 on its own path; this rule is the default-mode coalesce semantics.
rationale: D50; the INVALIDATE-side analogue of D44 (async×PAUSE). Prevents a spurious recompute against a vanished input — a redundant undirty RESOLVED (guarded fn) or a spurious terminal ERROR (non-guarding fn → panic → D30). Attributed cancellation preserves multi-dep updates (no lost update). Formal wave_paused_invalidate.tla (ChangedImpliesLive + PendingReflectsChanges + NoAllSentinelRecompute), TLC-green + mutation-verified. FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-29 on the TS+Rust-arms-green + formal precedent (C-13 ts:pass+rust:pass, both impl-fixes teeth-verified); py arm CSP-7.

statement: A dep's TERMINAL (COMPLETE/ERROR) RELEASES that dep's outstanding in-wave DIRTY contribution: if the dep went DIRTY this wave (phase 1) and has NOT yet settled with DATA/RESOLVED, the receiving node clears that dep's dirty flag and decrements its pending count — exactly as the DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE arms do. This is the EXACTLY-ONE-SETTLE invariant: every dep that goes DIRTY in phase 1 has its contribution released in phase 2 by exactly one settle-class event in {DATA, RESOLVED, INVALIDATE, COMPLETE, ERROR}. It applies in the ABSORBED-terminal cases where the node stays live — completeWhenDepsComplete:false (last/reduce, the *Map higher-order operators) and errorWhenDepsError:false (rescue/catch, R-deps-terminal); the AUTO-CASCADE cases (completeWhenDepsComplete && all deps complete -> node COMPLETE; errorWhenDepsError && a dep errors -> node ERROR) make the node itself terminal, so pending is moot there. If releasing the terminal dep's contribution drains pending to 0 while the node has already broadcast DIRTY this wave AND no terminal cascade fires, the node SETTLES: it recomputes (-> DATA from the remaining live deps' latest values) or, producing no tier-3 value, the substrate synthesizes exactly one undirty RESOLVED (R-resolved-undirty) to balance the downstream DIRTY. WITHOUT this release, a dep that emits DIRTY-then-COMPLETE/ERROR-without-a-value strands pending>0 -> the node never recomputes/settles and the DIRTY it broadcast wedges the downstream cone (the deadlock R-invalidate-idempotent already prevents for the INVALIDATE case). Restores R-diamond / R-two-phase for a diamond whose one leg terminates mid-wave. SCOPE: COMPLETE/ERROR only; a TEARDOWN arriving at a dirtied dep is the terminal-relay question (R-teardown-complete / B33), out of scope here.
rationale: surfaced by the CSP-2.7 /qa (edge-case review of the *Map operators): node._receiveFromDep's COMPLETE/ERROR arms did not clear a dep's dirty contribution the way the DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE arms do, so a DIRTY-then-terminal-without-DATA dep wedged a multi-dep node (B35). Pins TERMINAL as a settle-class event for dirty-accounting — the missing exactly-one-settle invariant — mirroring the INVALIDATE wedge-guard (the EC3 fix). Locked via /design-review (recommendation A-via-partial-C: a shared release-dirty + post-settle-undirty helper called by COMPLETE/ERROR alongside DATA/RESOLVED). PRE-EXISTING latent gap since CSP-1 (NOT introduced by D47); parity-consistent — the Rust dep-terminal receive arm is not yet built (node.rs _ => {}), so lock-BEFORE-build. No new D# (a dirty-accounting clarification of the two-phase contract D9, surfaced under D30 terminal handling). Formal: wave_terminal_dirty.tla (PendingCountsDirty + NoWedge, mutation-verified — dropping the terminal's release trips PendingCountsDirty). FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-30 on the TS-arm-green + formal precedent (R-rewire/R-reentrancy/R-rewire-deferred): TS impl = node.ts _receiveFromDep COMPLETE/ERROR arms _releaseDepDirty(idx) + _settleAfterAbsorbedTerminal (sawData→recompute, else undirty RESOLVED) / _maybeRun for terminalAsRealInput; C-15 ts:pass (a/b/c). rust:todo = the CSP-6 dep-terminal slice (builds the propagation machinery WITH the release first time, lock-before-build); py:todo CSP-7.

statement: Pull-mode nodes/self-holding retained views are quiet by default: while quiet they absorb upstream DIRTY/settle without relaying a downstream DIRTY, retaining/coalescing state according to their helper policy. PULL({pullId,params?}) is the only demand message and routes up the declared dep cone to the pullId holder; RESUME is pause-lock release only. When an accepted PULL is serviceable (settle-ready, or after an owed in-flight dep settles), the holder fn is invoked exactly once with ctx.pull/PullDemand installed, then the holder re-quiets after the service path. The substrate must not skip holder invocation merely because no dependency changed since the last demand. If the holder emits downstream DATA, it is ordinary ctx.down output and must be DIRTY-before-DATA. The substrate does not force a cached DATA output merely because PULL arrived. Plain pull snapshot helpers may therefore be silent on no-change demands, while parameterized retained views may compute and emit a page/snapshot from ctx.pull.params plus retained state/cursor even when no dependency changed. PULL params are holder-visible demand context only: they are not DATA-up, not independently emitted downstream, and not a second snapshot channel. If PULL arrives while the holder is not settle-ready, it becomes an owed demand; later separate PULLs before service overwrite the owed params (latest owed params wins) and still produce at most one holder invocation. Duplicate same-routed-wave arrivals at a holder are consumed idempotently by R-up-routing-diamond.
rationale: D55 introduced quiet pull nodes as the wedge fix; D269 split demand from RESUME into explicit PULL({pullId,params?}); D272 exposed params as holder context rather than a command or DATA-up path. D278 separates holder invocation from downstream output so retained views can answer parameterized PULLs over stable retained state/cursors without violating the no-hidden-read/no-DATA-up rules, while preserving no automatic push, no RESUME-demand shim, owed-latest params, and DIRTY-before-DATA for any emitted result.

statement: Up-going control/demand messages (R-ctx-up) route along DECLARED dep-edges. ctx.up(msgs) broadcasts up ALL deps; ctx.up(towardDep, msgs) routes up ONE declared edge (directed -- prunes other branches; also for branch-targeted PAUSE/RESUME/PULL/INVALIDATE). RESUME routing is pause-lock release only: RELEASE-IF-PAUSE-LOCK-HELD-ELSE-FORWARD-UP, and if no node up the cone holds the pause lock it drops at the depless terminus (net no-op). RESUME never fires a pull node. PULL routing is DEMAND-IF-PULL-HOLDER-ELSE-FORWARD-UP: a node holding the pullId consumes the PULL locally, receives params, fires the pull demand per R-pull, and does NOT forward; a node not holding the pullId forwards the PULL up its deps (broadcast or the single towardDep edge) to find the holder. This makes demand a cone-routed PULL({pullId, params?}) that travels up declared edges (inspectable, wave-ordered) WITHOUT the demander holding the target's reference; the pullId disambiguates which holder fires (siblings up one branch are told apart by identity). PAUSE stays node-targeted for acquisition (it creates a lock, so there is no pre-existing holder to find). DIRTY/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN forward toward deps to the depless-source terminus (R-up-at-source). A forwarded PULL whose pullId no node up the cone holds reaches the source terminus and is DROPPED (net no-op). INTRA-graph only (D22).
rationale: D59 made demand inspectable by routing it up declared edges but overloaded RESUME. D269 keeps declared-cone routing and node-reference avoidance while splitting demand into explicit PULL. This preserves pause/resume lock semantics, makes parameterized demand possible, and prevents accidental pause release from snapshot/retained-view pulls.

statement: A broadcast routed PULL({pullId, params?}) over a DAG is idempotent per pullId-holder per routed control/demand wave. If the same holder is reachable through multiple declared paths, it fires at most once for that PULL wave; duplicate same-wave arrivals at the already-fired holder are consumed silently and do not trigger a second pull delivery. The first delivered params for the holder in that routed wave are the holder-visible params; duplicate same-wave PULLs with conflicting params to the same holder are a DataIssue/design error at the helper layer and must not cause multiple deliveries. This same-wave first-params rule is distinct from R-pull latest-owed-params across separate later PULL demands before an owed demand delivers. This is a routing guarantee, not a reliance on R-pull's quiet coalescing after the first delivery. Directed ctx.up(towardDep,msgs) may still prune to one branch when the author wants a single path.
rationale: D63 / B47 pinned holder idempotence for routed RESUME demand. D269 revises the demand message to PULL and preserves the per-holder once-per-wave guarantee, now including a params discipline for duplicate arrivals.

statement: A substrate-synthesized undirty RESOLVED used to balance a previously broadcast DIRTY follows normal tier-3/4 delivery timing. In pausable:true default mode it may deliver immediately even while a pause lock is held; in pausable:'resumeAll' it is buffered and replayed on final-lock RESUME; inside an open batch it is deferred until the outermost batch commit. This applies to undirty RESOLVED produced by terminal dirty-release (R-terminal-settles-dirty) and by INVALIDATE dirty-clear paths. Implementations must not bypass the normal delivery path with a bare subscriber send for these balancing RESOLVEDs.
rationale: D64 / B39. Non-paused terminal dirty-release is already correct under C-15; the latent gap is only resumeAll/batch timing. Routing the balancing RESOLVED through normal delivery preserves D50 default-mode immediacy while honoring R-pause-modes and R-wave-boundary.

statement: TEARDOWN relays through an already-terminal intermediate. A terminal node receiving upstream TEARDOWN forwards TEARDOWN downstream without emitting a new COMPLETE/ERROR, without clearing terminal, and without allowing post-terminal DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR. A non-terminal node receiving TEARDOWN keeps R-teardown-complete behavior: synthesize COMPLETE before TEARDOWN unless the same wave already carries COMPLETE/ERROR. TEARDOWN is a destroy/unwire cascade, not a value/lifecycle resurrection.
rationale: D65 / B33. terminal-is-forever seals value output, but bridge/resource unwire must still reach downstream subscribers. Dropping TEARDOWN at a terminal guard leaks resources; relaying TEARDOWN is a narrow exception that does not reopen the node.

statement: A ctx captured by an async pool callback routes through the node's LIVE topology at emission time. If the node is rewired after the async invocation starts and before the callback calls ctx.up/ctx.down, the callback observes the current dep set/fn shape, not an invocation-time dep snapshot. Removed deps are drained and receive no late ctx traffic; added deps participate if they are live at emission time. Terminal output guards still seal post-terminal down emission.
rationale: D66 / B17. Live-edge ctx matches graph-first inspection and current TS behavior: describe shows live deps, and hidden invocation-snapshot edges would be invisible topology. Async remains outside the sync wave core; the callback re-enters through the normal live node boundary.

statement: If replaceDeps/subscribeDep/unsubscribeDep is requested while an outer batch is open and the target node has an uncommitted batched tier-3/4 settle slice, the rewire is accepted but deferred until after the outermost batch commits. The pending batched wave commits first against the pre-rewire topology/fn shape; then queued rewire requests drain FIFO as fresh boundary waves. Topology mutation never applies to an uncommitted batch view, and old-shape pending DATA is never committed against the new dep set. Outside an open batch, immediate/external rewire remains immediate between waves.
rationale: D67 / B19. This aligns external/immediate rewire with ctx.rewireNext's committed-boundary discipline while avoiding both a special reject and the unsafe rewire-before-commit ordering. Batch owns the current wave; topology changes begin after that wave commits.
